The existing sqlite_master name probe then handles detection, and an old file can never pass the swap check. The cost is the named ceiling below.\n- **A content-based gate:** sample index ids at Engine start and check that they exist in `video_embeddings`. Rejected because a missing id is the accepted stale-index state, not an error. It cannot tell a rowid index from a stale `ann_id` index, and it adds startup I/O. The sidecar `id_source` is cheap and exact.\n- **Put the id-source check in `server.py` only.** Rejected because `precompute-similar-ann.py` searches the same index. The shared `assert_index_matches_embeddings` covers both callers with one check.\n- **Keep the seed key named `rowid` but fill it with `ann_id`.** Rejected because the name would lie. The rename's main risk, a partial rename, is closed by a grep over `engine/server` and by the AC8 and existing similar tests.\n- **Sample training vectors by `ann_id % step` too.** That would work equally well, since hashes are uniform. It was not chosen only to keep the diff minimal and leave `fetch_training_samples` alone (see Tradeoffs).\n- **The conftest `compute_ann_id` re-export.** Rejected for the reason given under Test import pattern above.\n- **Gate first, then readers.** Rejected because every phase-1 and phase-2 checkpoint would then run against an Engine that refuses the shared dataset's index. With readers first, no earlier checkpoint goes red when a later phase lands.\n\n### Gotchas, risks and limitations\n\n- **The crash window inside the build.** `build-ann-index.py` writes the index before the sidecar. The one-time window is a cutover build that dies between the two writes: it leaves a new `ann_id` index under the old `rowid` sidecar, the gate refuses it, and the updater's `finally` restart fails loudly rather than serving wrong videos. After the cutover, every index and sidecar pairing on disk is `ann_id`-keyed, so a failed build leaves at worst a stale index, never a wrong one.\n- **An old-shape DB under an `ann_id` sidecar.** One example is a pre-migration backup restored under a post-cutover index. The gate passes on the sidecar, and the readers then fail per query with `no such column: ann_id`. That is a loud error, not a wrong video. AC5 asks for no startup DB-shape check, so I add none. `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(server.db)` at start would be the one-line upgrade if wanted.\n- **Partial rename.** A forgotten `seed.get(\"rowid\")` silently disables self-exclusion, and `seed[\"rowid\"]` raises KeyError.   "draft": "## Draft: plan B, readers and cutover on `ann_id`\n\nI read every production file the plan touches: `ann_ids.py`, `build-ann-index.py`, `embedding_space.py`, `ann.py`, `embeddings.py`, `metadata.py`, `search.vector_candidates`, `similar._handle_vector_search`, `random_cache.py`, `random_videos.fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, `precompute-random-rowids.py`, `precompute-similar-ann.py` and the smoke test's `validate_outputs`. I also read the test harnesses I extend: `test_precompute_similar_ann.py`, `test_precompute_random_rowids.py`, `test_random_cache.py`'s engines test, the `_CHILD` in `test_search.py`, and `sync_job` and `similars_stack` in `test_video.py`. A `rowid` count over `engine/server/**/*.py` matches the inventory file for file.\n\nLadder: no new module beyond the two tests and no new dependency. Every change is a rename or rekey of code that already exists. The gate reuses the model check's shape, and old-shape cache detection reuses the existing `sqlite_master` name probe (rung 2). Converged in one pass.\n\n### What the build has to test\n\n| Behaviour | Where it is observed |\n|---|---|\n| The index stores exactly the DB's `ann_id` set; the sidecar `id_source` is `ANN_ID_SOURCE`; an old six-column table is refused naming `migrate-whitelist.py` (AC4) | `tests/active/test_ann_ids.py`: job subprocess, then an ENGINE_PY reader child |\n| The gate passes the written sidecar and refuses `video_embeddings.rowid` and a missing `id_source`, naming `build-ann-index.py` (AC5) | `test_ann_ids.py`, in-process (`embedding_space` is stdlib plus `data.ann_ids`) |\n| Similar and vector search resolve each hit to the video its id was built from, after a reverse reinsert, a host purge and a new video, with no index rebuild (AC8) | `tests/active/test_stale_ann_index.py`, ENGINE_PY `_CHILD` |\n| Similarity precompute neighbours resolve by `ann_id`; no source lists itself (AC7) | `test_precompute_similar_ann.py` |\n| The random cache is `random_ann_ids`, ids come from the source, and an old `random_rowids` `--out` at size is rebuilt (AC6) | `test_precompute_random_rowids.py`, `test_random_cache.py`, `test_db.py`, `test_random_videos.py` |\n| `fetch_metadata` resolves by `ann_id`, and its output keys are unchanged | `test_metadata.py` (`ROW_KEYS`) |\n| The full cycle writes the `ann_id` sidecar (AC9) | `test-orchestrator-smoke.py`, run manually |\n\n### Module map\n\n#### `engine/server/data/ann_ids.py` (phase 3)\nAdd next to `ANN_ID_MASK`. The module stays stdlib-only.\n```python\n# The sidecar id_source of an index whose FAISS ids are ann_id; build-ann-index.py writes it, embedding_space and the smoke test check it.\nANN_ID_SOURCE = \"video_embeddings.ann_id\"\n```\n\n#### `engine/server/db/jobs/build-ann-index.py` (phase 3)\n```python\nfrom data.ann_ids import ANN_ID_SOURCE, assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id\nfrom data.embedding_space import resolve_embedding_space\n\n@dataclass\nclass EmbeddingRow:\n    \"\"\"Represent embedding row behavior.\"\"\"\n    ann_id: int\n    embedding: np.ndarray\n\n# iter_embeddings\n        for ann_id, embedding_blob, embedding_dim in rows:\n            ...\n            batch.append(EmbeddingRow(ann_id=ann_id, embedding=embedding))\n\n# main()\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    # Refused before anything is built: a table without ann_id would give an index the readers cannot resolve.\n    assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(conn)\n\n    dim, model_name = resolve_embedding_space(conn)\n    ...\n    query = \"SELECT ann_id, embedding, embedding_dim FROM video_embeddings\"\n    for batch in iter_embeddings(conn, query, (), dim, args.batch_size):\n        ids = np.array([item.ann_id for item in batch], dtype=np.int64)\n    ...\n        \"id_source\": ANN_ID_SOURCE,\n```\n- Invariant: every id is in 1..2^63-1, because of the mask and the CHECK, so int64 holds it.\n- The write order stays index first, then sidecar.\n- `fetch_training_samples` is left untouched (named simplification).\n\n#### `engine/server/data/embedding_space.py` (phase 3)\nDocstring paragraph appended after \"These helpers are the readers of that record.\":\n> FAISS ids are `video_embeddings.ann_id` (ADR-0006), derived from each video's key rather than its row position. An index the table has since moved on from can therefore only miss a video, never name the wrong one. The sidecar records this as `id_source`, and an index with any other id source, such as the earlier rowid ids, is refused rather than read.\n\nImport `from data.ann_ids import ANN_ID_SOURCE`, then add after the model check:\n```python\n    index_id_source = str(meta.get(\"id_source\") or \"\")\n    if index_id_source != ANN_ID_SOURCE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            f\"Index ids come from {index_id_source or '<unset>'} but the readers resolve \"\n            f\"{ANN_ID_SOURCE}. WHERE ann_id IN` and returns `{row[\"ann_id\"]: dict(row)}`. `fetch_similarity_targets_chunked(conn, ann_ids, chunk_size=5000)` only has its parameters renamed.\n- The two selection queries use `SELECT e.ann_id`, giving `pending_ann_ids = [int(row[\"ann_id\"]) ...]`, then `iter_embedding_rows_by_ann_ids(src_db, pending_ann_ids)`. The comment at line 366 becomes \"only ANN ids are materialized\".\n- The full mode uses `SELECT ann_id, video_id, instance_domain, embedding, embedding_dim`.\n- The batch uses `batch_ann_ids` and `targets_by_ann_id`, and the loop reads `ann_id_int = int(ann_id); if ann_id_int == row[\"ann_id\"] or ann_id_int <= 0: continue`.\n- The `video_keys`/`similarity_sources` joins, `write_similarities`, the `mode=ro` source and the gate call are untouched.\n\n#### `engine/server/data/random_cache.py` (phase 2)\n```python\nRANDOM_CACHE_CHECK_SQL = \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM random_ann_ids\"\n\ndef ensure_random_cache_schema(conn):\n    conn.executescript(\"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS random_ann_ids (\n          position INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n          ann_id INTEGER NOT NULL\n        );\n        \"\"\")\n\ndef random_ann_ids_count(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the number of cached ANN ids, or None when the random_ann_ids table is missing, as in a cache written before the ANN-id cutover (random_rowids).\"\"\"\n    # fetchall, so no statement is left holding SHARED on the file.\n    if not conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'random_ann_ids' LIMIT 1\").fetchall():\n        return None\n    return int(conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM random_ann_ids\").fetchall()[0][0])\n```\n`populate_random_cache`:\n- The reuse check uses `random_ann_ids_count`, and the count and delete run on `random_ann_ids`.\n- The source stats query is `SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, MIN(ann_id) AS min_id, MAX(ann_id) AS max_id FROM video_embeddings`.\n- The unfiltered window is `SELECT ann_id FROM video_embeddings WHERE ann_id >= ? Every reader, the random cache and the index build resolve through `video_embeddings.ann_id`. `ANN_ID_SOURCE` and `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id` each live in one place, `data/ann_ids.py`, and the index build, the startup gate and the smoke test import them from there. A grep across the repo for the old names (`exclude_rowid`, `ann_rowids`, `video_rowid`, `random_rowids_count`, `fetch_random_rowids`, `iter_embedding_rows_by_rowids`) finds no live code reference. The only hits are plans and records, the deliberate old-format `random_rowids` probe in tests/active/test_random_cache.py, and tests/tmp checkpoint files.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nThe private `set_nprobe` in engine/server/db/jobs/precompute-similar-ann.py is a copy of `data.ann.apply_nprobe`. I left it alone for two reasons. It predates this build. And the job cannot import `data.ann` at the top of the module: `data.ann` imports `data.metadata`, which imports `recommendations.keys`, and that lives under `api/`, which the job only adds to `sys.path` inside `main()`. Removing the copy means moving that path setup, which is a structural change for its own step. Also left alone: `_chunk` is copied in data/embeddings.py and data/metadata.py, and `fetch_embeddings_by_ids` has its own embeddings SELECT. Both predate this build and neither is touched by its intent. In random_cache.py I did not swap `populate_random_cache`'s inline `SELECT COUNT(*) ... fetchone()` for `random_ann_ids_count`. The swap adds a `sqlite_master` query to the locked rebuild path, which the 6 s lock-wait test measures, and saves only one line. I also did not rename the job file `precompute-random-rowids.py`: the plan keeps its name and arguments, and the orchestrator and test groups call it by that name. The searches were static (Grep only); I made no test run in this pass.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nnone\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nStatic searches found no leftover rowid-era names in live code and only pre-existing duplication, none of which can be removed safely inside this build, so the refactor pass changed nothing.\n</observation>"

## 2026-10-02 - Step 1 - Gather requirements

Approved by the operator.

### requirements

### Asked for

Issue `docs/project/issues/08-stable-ann-ids.md` (roadmap F1-M2), the second of two builds. Plan 17 (`docs/project/plans/17-stable-ann-ids.md`) went through build 19 up to its Step 6. It was then split into plan A (`docs/project/plans/41-ann-ids-a-schema-writers.md`, built in record `docs/project/plans/43-41-ann-ids-a-schema-writers.record.md`) and this plan B (`docs/project/plans/42-ann-ids-b-readers-cutover.md`, built in record `docs/project/plans/44-42-ann-ids-b-readers-cutover.record.md`). ADR-0006 (`docs/project/adr/0006-derived-ann-ids.md`) records the id decision, and `CONTEXT.md` defines **ANN id**.

Plan B moves the FAISS index, and every reader that turns an id back into an embedded video, from `video_embeddings.rowid` to the `ann_id` that plan A stores. It also makes the Engine refuse a rowid index. This plan is the cutover: its readers, its index build and its gate merge together.

The operator confirmed in this Step 1 that plan A is complete in this worktree. Plan A's code is the base plan B builds on, and the single merge of this worktree carries both plans. Everything else was settled with the operator in build 19 (Steps 1-5; that record is now in `delete_me/`), narrowed to plan B. The operator approved these requirements in this Step 1.

### Purpose

Correctness. `video_embeddings` can change without an index rebuild following, or while the rebuild fails: a merge, a host purge, a whole-table reload, a `--force` re-embed, a migration. In every such case the index must never return the wrong video. At most it misses videos it has not indexed yet. The build must not block later incremental index add or remove (F3/F4-M2), and it does not build them.

### Acceptance criteria

- **AC4, the index build.**
  - `build-ann-index.py` calls `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(conn)` right after connecting and before `resolve_embedding_space`. When the column is missing, it fails with plan A's message, which names `migrate-whitelist.py`.
  - It adds vectors with `ann_id` as their FAISS ids: the add query becomes `SELECT ann_id, embedding, embedding_dim FROM video_embeddings`, `EmbeddingRow.rowid` becomes `ann_id`, and the ids are built as `np.int64`.
  - It writes `id_source: "video_embeddings.ann_id"` (`ANN_ID_SOURCE`) to the sidecar.
  - `fetch_training_samples` keeps `rowid % step`. It is a sampling cursor, never an identity, and that is a named simplification.
- **AC5, the Engine gate.**
  - `assert_index_matches_embeddings` raises RuntimeError when the sidecar's `id_source` is not `video_embeddings.ann_id`, a missing `id_source` included. The check sits next to the model check, and it refuses the same way the model check does.
  - The message says what is wrong (the index's id source, or `<unset>`, against the `ann_id` source the readers resolve) and names `build-ann-index.py`.
  - The Engine therefore refuses to start on a rowid index, and `precompute-similar-ann.py` refuses one too.
  - The module docstring gains the id contract.
- **AC6, the readers.** These resolve embedded videos by `ann_id`:
  - **Similar.**
    - The seed keys `rowid` and `exclude_rowid` become `ann_id` and `exclude_ann_id` in all of `resolve_seed`'s return shapes and in `_seed_from_row`. The four `e.rowid AS rowid` selects in `embeddings.py` become `e.ann_id AS ann_id`.
    - The ANN results in `ann.py` move: `compute_similar_items` (the `> 0` filter stays, and its self check uses `seed["ann_id"]`), `search_similar_above` (`seed.get("ann_id")`, with the `> 0` filter kept), and `search_index`, whose fourth positional parameter becomes `exclude_ann_id`.
    - `similar._handle_vector_search` moves too.
    - Every consumer of the seed keys is renamed together: `ann.py`, `similar.py`, `similarity_candidates`, and the recommendation sources `ann_similar_from_likes.py` and `cached_similar_from_likes.py` that pass seeds through.
  - **Search.** The vector half of search (`search.vector_candidates`) moves.
  - **Metadata.** `fetch_metadata(conn, ann_ids, ...)` uses `e.ann_id AS ann_id ... WHERE e.ann_id IN (...)`, served by the UNIQUE index. Its output dicts still carry no id.
  - **Random cache.** `random_cache.py`, `random_videos.py` and `precompute-random-rowids.py` move. The table becomes `random_ann_ids (position INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ann_id INTEGER NOT NULL)`, and the helpers are renamed:
    - `random_rowids_count` becomes `random_ann_ids_count`;
    - `fetch_random_rowids` becomes `fetch_random_ann_ids`.
    `RANDOM_CACHE_CHECK_SQL` names the new table. The unfiltered build draws a random start in `[MIN(ann_id), MAX(ann_id)]`, then takes the next rows in `ann_id` order with wrap-around. The filtered `scan_range` ranges over `ann_id`.
  - **Old-shape random cache.** A stored cache in the old `random_rowids` shape is detected and repopulated, never read:
    - `random_ann_ids_count` returns None on it, so `open_random_cache_if_usable` returns None and the Engine starts a background build.
    - The precompute keep check counts 0, so the job rebuilds.
    - A swap can only install a file holding `random_ann_ids`.
    Detection is by table name, not by shape. That is a named simplification. Its ceiling: a future reshape under the same name would need a `PRAGMA table_info` check in `random_ann_ids_count`.
  - **End state.** Afterwards no reader resolves an embedded video by rowid.
- **AC7, the similarity precompute.**
  - `precompute-similar-ann.py` uses `ann_id` for its FAISS ids and its target lookup:
    - `iter_embedding_rows_by_rowids` becomes `iter_embedding_rows_by_ann_ids`;
    - `fetch_similarity_targets*` take `ann_ids` and return `{ann_id: row}`;
    - the pending-selection queries and the full-mode SELECT carry `ann_id`;
    - self-exclusion becomes `ann_id_int == row["ann_id"]`.
  - Its output keys and its incremental selection stay on `(video_id, instance_domain)` and the `video_keys` joins.
  - Its source connection stays `mode=ro` and registers nothing.
- **AC8, the purpose observed in a test.**
  - Build an index on `ann_id`. Then, with no index rebuild, run three cases: (A) delete every row and reinsert them in reverse order, (B) purge a host through `purge_host_data`, (C) insert a new, unindexed video.
  - After each case, every hit from similar (`ann.compute_similar_items`) and from search (`search.vector_candidates`) resolves to the video whose vector carries that id, or is dropped.
  - The purged host's videos are absent, and the new video is absent rather than substituted.
- **AC9, the cycle and docs (plan B's part).**
  - The updater's full cycle (merge, ANN build, precompute) runs on the new id source. That is observed through the orchestrator smoke test: `validate_outputs` asserts `meta.get("id_source") == ANN_ID_SOURCE` next to the `meta_total` check and records `checks["ann_id_source"]`.
  - The docs carry three things: the cutover (stop the Engine, run `build-ann-index.py`, start), the startup refusal, and the random cache's `random_ann_ids` shape.

### Scope

**In scope:**
- AC4-AC8 and plan B's part of AC9.
- Adding `ANN_ID_SOURCE = "video_embeddings.ann_id"` to `engine/server/data/ann_ids.py`, which is the one place the sidecar value is defined.

- The issue closes with this plan.

**Out of scope:**
- Everything plan A delivered: the id, the schema, the migration, the writers and the mini-prod guards.
- Promoting plan A's `tests/tmp/test_41_*` checkpoints into `tests/active`, and plan A's doc changes. They remain plan A's.
- Incremental FAISS add or remove (F3/F4-M2).
- The similarity cache, `videos_fts` and the crawler.
- Backward compatibility with rowid indexes. A `rowid` sidecar is refused, not read.

### Consistency constraints

- Job CLIs keep their current arguments. `precompute-random-rowids.py` keeps its file name; only its description and `--size` help text change.
- Refusal messages follow `data/embedding_space.py`: say what is wrong, and name the command that fixes it.
- New code matches the style of the file it lands in.
- Every id comes from plan A's `compute_ann_id`, or from the stored `ann_id`. `ANN_ID_SOURCE` is the only spelling of the sidecar value, used by `build-ann-index.py`, `embedding_space.py` and the smoke test.
- `data/ann_ids.py` stays stdlib-only (plus `data.moderation`), so jobs and tests on the system interpreter (`test_precompute_random_rowids` runs the job under `sys.executable`) can import it.
- Ids up to 2^63 exceed JavaScript's safe integer range. No response puts an `ann_id` into JSON; if one ever does, it must be a string.
- Tests that need `compute_ann_id` use one pattern. Either they follow `test_video.py` (insert `engine/server` on `sys.path`, then `from data.ann_ids import compute_ann_id`), or Step 5 adds the `compute_ann_id` re-export to conftest that plan A planned. They are not mixed.
- Smallest thing that works: no new module beyond the tests, and no new dependency.

### Conflicts

- **One merge, not three.** Readers on `ann_id` against a rowid index return wrong videos, and so does an `ann_id` index against rowid readers. The three phases therefore land in one build and one merge, and no phase is merged alone. Readers come before the gate so that no earlier checkpoint goes red when a later phase lands.

### Risks and limitations accepted

- **Hard cutover.** The Engine refuses a `rowid` sidecar, so the deploy is stop, `build-ann-index.py`, start. The similarity cache needs no rebuild, and the random cache rebuilds itself.
- **Purged or deleted videos** stay in the index until the next rebuild. They come back as misses (no metadata row), never as wrong videos.
- **A re-embedded video** keeps its old vector in the index until the next rebuild, but still resolves to the right video.
- **New videos** stay out of the index until a rebuild.
- **The unfiltered random draw** becomes a hash-uniform sample rather than a block of rows in insertion order.
- **Partial seed-key rename.** `seed.get("rowid")` silently stops self-exclusion, and `seed["rowid"]` raises KeyError. Every consumer is renamed together.
- **A missed `rowid` in `build-ann-index.py`** produces an index the gate accepts by its sidecar but with wrong ids. The AC4 test compares the stored id set with the DB's `ann_id` set.
- **ANN training** samples by `rowid % step`, which affects only which vectors train the quantizer.
- **Random-cache detection** is by table name.

### Coordination the operator does

- **Before the final full-suite run,** with the Engine stopped: run `engine/server/db/jobs/migrate-whitelist.py` on the shared dataset if it has not been run yet, then `build-ann-index.py`, then start the Engine.
- **The smoke test's `id_source` assertion** needs a migrated `--source-db`. The operator runs it manually.

## 2026-10-02 - Step 2 - Develop a solution

Approved by the operator.

### initial_solution

### Approach

Plan B is a rename-and-rekey of every place that turns a FAISS id back into a video. It puts the readers, the index build and the Engine gate onto the `ann_id` that plan A already stores, and merges them as one unit. I read the tree to confirm the settled current state: `ann_ids.py` as delivered, `build-ann-index.py`, `embedding_space.py`, `ann.py`, `embeddings.py`, `metadata.py`, `search.vector_candidates`, `random_cache.py`, `random_videos.fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, `precompute-random-rowids.py` and the `precompute-similar-ann.py` selection and target code. Two findings narrow the work:

- The recommendation sources (`ann_similar_from_likes.py`, `cached_similar_from_likes.py`) and `similarity_candidates` never read an id key. They only pass the seed dict on to `compute_similar_items` or the handler. So "renaming every consumer together" means editing the producers (`embeddings.py`) and the readers of the key (`ann.py`, `similar.py`), plus a grep that proves no other `"rowid"` or `"exclude_rowid"` key reader is left under `engine/server/api` and `engine/server/data`.
- No response carries an id. The handler sends `seed["meta"]` as the JSON `seed` payload, and it holds only `video_id`, `instance_domain`, `channel_id` and `title`. `fetch_metadata`'s output dicts carry no id. The JS safe-integer constraint therefore holds with no extra work.

**AC4, the index build.** In `build-ann-index.py`:

- `main()` calls `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(conn)` right after `sqlite3.connect`, before `resolve_embedding_space`. An old six-column table fails with plan A's message, which names `migrate-whitelist.py`.
- `EmbeddingRow.rowid` becomes `ann_id`, and `iter_embeddings` unpacks `ann_id`.
- The add query selects `ann_id, embedding, embedding_dim`. The ids array stays `np.int64`, and every `ann_id` fits there because it is masked to 63 bits and positive by CHECK.
- The sidecar's `id_source` is the new constant `ANN_ID_SOURCE` from `data/ann_ids.py`. That constant is one string, so the module stays stdlib-only.
- `fetch_training_samples` is left on `rowid % step`, a named simplification (see Tradeoffs).

**AC5, the Engine gate.** `assert_index_matches_embeddings` imports `ANN_ID_SOURCE` and checks `meta.get("id_source")` right after the model check:

- The check is written in the same style as the model check. The message names the index's source, or `<unset>` when the key is missing, says the readers resolve `video_embeddings.ann_id`, and tells the operator to rebuild the index with `build-ann-index.py`.
- The function's two callers (`api/server.py` at start and `precompute-similar-ann.py`) both get the refusal without being touched.
- The module docstring gains one paragraph on the id contract: FAISS ids are `video_embeddings.ann_id`, a stale index can only miss, and any other source is refused.

**AC6, the readers.**

- **`embeddings.py`.** The four `e.rowid AS rowid` selects become `e.ann_id AS ann_id`, and `_seed_from_row` returns `"ann_id"`. Every return shape of `resolve_seed` changes `exclude_rowid` to `exclude_ann_id` and `rowid` to `ann_id`: the zero vector, the parsed vector, the not-found case and the found seed.
- **`ann.py`.**
  - `compute_similar_items` keeps the `> 0` filter, renames its locals and the log key to `ann_ids`, and self-excludes on `seed["ann_id"]`.
  - `search_similar_above` uses `seed.get("ann_id")` and keeps `> 0`.
  - `search_index`'s fourth positional parameter becomes `exclude_ann_id`.
- **The vector search callers.** `similar._handle_vector_search` passes `seed["exclude_ann_id"]`, and `search.vector_candidates` renames its locals. Both already pass ids straight to `fetch_metadata`.
- **`fetch_metadata`.** It takes `ann_ids`, selects `e.ann_id AS ann_id`, filters `WHERE e.ann_id IN (...)` (served by plan A's UNIQUE `idx_video_embeddings_ann_id`) and keys its result by `ann_id`. The output dicts are unchanged.
- **The random cache.**
  - `ensure_random_cache_schema` creates `random_ann_ids (position INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ann_id INTEGER NOT NULL)`, and `RANDOM_CACHE_CHECK_SQL` counts that table.
  - `random_rowids_count` becomes `random_ann_ids_count`. It looks up `random_ann_ids` by name in `sqlite_master`, so an old file returns None.
  - `populate_random_cache` takes `MIN`/`MAX`/`COUNT` over `ann_id`. The unfiltered window is `ann_id >= start ORDER BY ann_id LIMIT n`, plus the wrap-around `ann_id < start`. The filtered `scan_range` ranges and orders over `e.ann_id` and advances with `ann_id + 1`. The scan is already a keyset cursor, not span arithmetic, so the sparse 63-bit id space costs nothing.
  - `fetch_random_rowids` becomes `fetch_random_ann_ids`, reading the `ann_id` column.
  - `random_videos.py` changes its import, its locals and its docstring.
  - `precompute-random-rowids.py` keeps its file name and arguments. It imports `random_ann_ids_count`, and only its description and its `--size` help text change.
  - The comment in `server_config.py` changes.
- **Old-shape random caches.** Each path is covered by code that already exists:
  - The Engine's `open_random_cache_if_usable` gets None, logs `no_table`, and `server.py:345` starts a background build. Random requests are served from the DB until the build lands.
  - The job's keep check counts `None or 0` and rebuilds into a fresh per-pid temp file, which then replaces `--out`. The result holds only `random_ann_ids`.
  - `swap_readonly_connection` validates with `RANDOM_CACHE_CHECK_SQL`, so it can install only the new shape.

**AC7, the similarity precompute.**

- `iter_embedding_rows_by_rowids` becomes `iter_embedding_rows_by_ann_ids` (`WHERE ann_id IN`).
- `fetch_similarity_targets` and `fetch_similarity_targets_chunked` take `ann_ids` and return `{ann_id: row}`.
- Both pending-selection queries select `e.ann_id`, and the full-mode SELECT reads `ann_id` instead of `rowid`.
- The main loop self-excludes on `ann_id_int == row["ann_id"]` and keeps `<= 0`.
- The `video_keys`/`similarity_sources` joins, the output keys and the `mode=ro` source connection are left alone.

**AC8, the purpose.** `tests/active/test_stale_ann_index.py` runs an ENGINE_PY `_CHILD`:

- It builds the tmp DB through `ensure_video_embeddings_schema` and an `IDMap2,IVF1,Flat` index on `ann_id`. With one list, the search is exact and deterministic.
- It records `ann_id -> (video_id, host)`, then runs cases A (delete all rows and reinsert them in reverse), B (`purge_host_data`) and C (insert one unindexed video).
- After each case it calls `compute_similar_items` and `vector_candidates` through a stub server.
- It asserts that every hit equals the recorded identity for the id that produced it. A rowid join would fail case A, because the reverse reinsert permutes the rowids.

**AC9, the smoke test and docs.**

- `validate_outputs` imports `ANN_ID_SOURCE` next to its existing `ensure_video_embeddings_schema` import. Beside the `meta_total` check it asserts `meta.get("id_source") == ANN_ID_SOURCE` and records `checks["ann_id_source"]`.
- The docs listed in the requirements gain the cutover sequence, the startup refusal and its triage row, the `migrate-whitelist.py` refusal of `build-ann-index`, and the `random_ann_ids` shape with its self-rebuild.
- The issue is set to `enhancement, complete` and archived.

**Test import pattern.** Every test that needs `compute_ann_id` follows `test_video.py`: it inserts `engine/server` on `sys.path`, then runs `from data.ann_ids import compute_ann_id`. `test_metadata`, `test_random_cache`, `test_random_videos`, `test_db` and `test_precompute_similar_ann` already insert `engine/server` and import from `data.*`, so for them this is a one-line import. A conftest re-export would put `engine/server` on the path for every test, and `test_video.py` notes that both trees hold a `server` module. That collision is avoided by not touching conftest.

**Phasing.** I keep the three phases from build 19 and the order readers, then random cache, then index build and gate, all in one merge:

- Phase 1 already writes `"id_source": "video_embeddings.ann_id"` into the `test_precompute_similar_ann` fixture sidecar, so phase 3's gate does not turn it red.
- The docs land with phase 3, since they describe the cutover that phase completes.

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep `rowid` as the FAISS id and add an id→key map table written at build time.** Rejected because ADR-0006 settles derived ids. A map also goes stale the same way rowids do, unless it is snapshotted with the index.
- **Store `(video_id, instance_domain)` in the random cache instead of ANN ids.** Rejected because it forks `fetch_metadata` into a second keyed path for one caller. The `ann_id` form reuses the single id→metadata path, and the UNIQUE index serves it.
- **Keep the table name `random_rowids` and rename only the column, detected via `PRAGMA table_info`.** Rejected in favour of a new table name. The existing sqlite_master name probe then handles detection, and an old file can never pass the swap check. The cost is the named ceiling below.
- **A content-based gate:** sample index ids at Engine start and check that they exist in `video_embeddings`. Rejected because a missing id is the accepted stale-index state, not an error. It cannot tell a rowid index from a stale `ann_id` index, and it adds startup I/O. The sidecar `id_source` is cheap and exact.
- **Put the id-source check in `server.py` only.** Rejected because `precompute-similar-ann.py` searches the same index. The shared `assert_index_matches_embeddings` covers both callers with one check.
- **Keep the seed key named `rowid` but fill it with `ann_id`.** Rejected because the name would lie. The rename's main risk, a partial rename, is closed by a grep over `engine/server` and by the AC8 and existing similar tests.
- **Sample training vectors by `ann_id % step` too.** That would work equally well, since hashes are uniform. It was not chosen only to keep the diff minimal and leave `fetch_training_samples` alone (see Tradeoffs).
- **The conftest `compute_ann_id` re-export.** Rejected for the reason given under Test import pattern above.
- **Gate first, then readers.** Rejected because every phase-1 and phase-2 checkpoint would then run against an Engine that refuses the shared dataset's index. With readers first, no earlier checkpoint goes red when a later phase lands.

### Gotchas, risks and limitations

- **The crash window inside the build.** `build-ann-index.py` writes the index before the sidecar. The one-time window is a cutover build that dies between the two writes: it leaves a new `ann_id` index under the old `rowid` sidecar, the gate refuses it, and the updater's `finally` restart fails loudly rather than serving wrong videos. After the cutover, every index and sidecar pairing on disk is `ann_id`-keyed, so a failed build leaves at worst a stale index, never a wrong one.
- **An old-shape DB under an `ann_id` sidecar.** One example is a pre-migration backup restored under a post-cutover index. The gate passes on the sidecar, and the readers then fail per query with `no such column: ann_id`. That is a loud error, not a wrong video. AC5 asks for no startup DB-shape check, so I add none. `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(server.db)` at start would be the one-line upgrade if wanted.
- **Partial rename.** A forgotten `seed.get("rowid")` silently disables self-exclusion, and `seed["rowid"]` raises KeyError. The rename lands in one phase, a grep checks it, and AC8 plus the similar tests exercise both paths.
- **A missed `rowid` in the index build** would pass the gate with wrong ids. The AC4 test compares `vector_to_array(index.id_map)` exactly with the DB's `ann_id` set.
- **Old caches left in place.** An in-place `populate_random_cache` on a file that still holds `random_rowids` (only the in-place tests do this) leaves that dead table next to `random_ann_ids`. Nothing reads it.
- **AC4 test parameters.** The default `--nlist 4096`/`--m 32` cannot train on a fixture of a few dozen vectors. The test passes small `--nlist`/`--m`/`--train-sample` values, and the job's CLI is unchanged.
- **The engine-backed suite fails until the dataset is cut over.** Once phase 3 lands, the shared `whitelist.db` and its index must be migrated and rebuilt before the full-suite run (operator coordination). The orchestrator smoke test likewise needs a migrated `--source-db` and is run manually.
- **Archived tests stay as they are.** `tests/archive/random_cache_in_place/test_random_cache.py` still names `random_rowids` and is not run.

### Tradeoffs the operator is asked to accept

- **A hard cutover.** A `rowid` sidecar is refused, so the deploy is: stop the Engine, run `build-ann-index.py`, start it. The similarity cache is untouched. The random cache rebuilds itself in the background, and until it does the random feed comes from the DB path.
- **Stale index behaviour.**
  - Purged or deleted videos stay in the index until the next rebuild and come back as misses.
  - Re-embedded videos keep their old vector, but it resolves to the right video.
  - New videos are absent until a rebuild.
- **The unfiltered random draw.** It becomes a hash-uniform window instead of a block of rows in insertion order. Ids that follow a large gap are a little more likely to start a window, which is negligible at a window of thousands.
- **Named simplification: training samples.** ANN training keeps sampling by `rowid % step`. That is a cursor that picks quantizer training vectors, never an identity. Its ceiling: a heavily fragmented rowid space could skew which vectors train the quantizer, which affects recall only, never correctness. The upgrade is one token, `ann_id % step`.
- **Named simplification: random-cache detection.** An old cache is recognised by its table name. Its ceiling: a future reshape under the name `random_ann_ids` would go undetected. The upgrade is a `PRAGMA table_info` column check in `random_ann_ids_count`.

<impact path="tests/active/test_stale_ann_index.py" element="new AC8 test (ENGINE_PY child)">
**What changes.** A new file. The child runs under `ENGINE_PY` (it needs faiss and numpy) with `engine/server` and `engine/server/api` on `sys.path`. `data.metadata` imports `recommendations.keys` from `api`, as `test_metadata.py:24-29` shows.

**Fixture:**

- An `IDMap2,IVF1,Flat` index built on `ann_id`.

**Cases:**
- **Case A:** delete and reinsert in reverse. Same keys, so the collision trigger does not fire.
- **Case B:** `purge_host_data(conn, host)` (`moderation.py:194`). It normalises the host and raises ValueError on an invalid one, and it runs its own `with conn:`.
- **Case C:** one unindexed insert.
- After each case, call `compute_similar_items` and `vector_candidates` through a stub server. The stub attributes are listed under `ann.py` and `search.py`. `vector_candidates` needs a stub `query_encoder`.

**What depends on it.** `tests/config.json` needs a new entry mapping it to `data/ann.py`, `data/metadata.py`, `data/search.py`, `data/embeddings.py` and `data/ann_ids.py`.

**Regression risk.** None to the product. The test's discriminating power rests on case A actually permuting rowids, which a control assertion should check.
</impact>
<impact path="tests/active/test_build_ann_index.py" element="new AC4/AC5 tests (location assumed; the plan names the checks, not the file)">
**AC4 checks:**
- `build-ann-index.py` run as an `ENGINE_PY` subprocess on a tmp DB built through `ensure_video_embeddings_schema`.
- `faiss.vector_to_array(index.id_map)` equals the DB's `ann_id` set.
- The sidecar's `id_source == ANN_ID_SOURCE`.
- An old six-column table exits non-zero with stderr naming `migrate-whitelist.py`.

**AC5 checks** on `assert_index_matches_embeddings`:
- a `video_embeddings.rowid` sidecar raises naming `build-ann-index.py`;
- a sidecar missing `id_source` raises with `<unset>`;
- the correct sidecar passes.

AC5 can run in-process, because `embedding_space` is stdlib-only plus `ann_ids`, and `index` can be a `SimpleNamespace(d=dim)`.

**Parameters.** The build needs `--cpu`, small `--nlist`, an `--m` that divides dim, a small `--nbits` (or at least 256 rows) and `--train-sample` of at least the row count. See the training-samples entry.

**Regression risk.** None to the product. A `tests/config.json` entry is needed.

### highest_risk


`tests/active/test_video.py` `similars_stack` (lines 216-219): it builds its FAISS index from `SELECT rowid` and is not named in the plan. Once `fetch_metadata` filters on `e.ann_id`, the similars-under-refresh case gets no neighbour and fails. It is the one test-side reader the plan's churn list misses.
`engine/server/data/ann.py` `search_similar_above` (line 112) and its producer `embeddings.resolve_seed`/`_seed_from_row`: a partial rename turns `seed.get("rowid")` into a silent None. Self-exclusion in the up-next fallback stops with no error, so only a test that asserts the seed is absent catches it. The `seed["rowid"]` and `seed["exclude_rowid"]` siblings fail loudly instead.
`engine/server/data/embedding_space.py` `assert_index_matches_embeddings`: the gate refuses every existing sidecar, so the whole Engine-backed suite and every prod instance stop at start until the shared `whitelist.db` is migrated and reindexed. A failed updater ANN build now means an Engine outage. A reindex from a worktree breaks main and other lanes, which have no gate and would serve empty results. The AC4 test also needs `--nbits`, or at least 256 rows, or IVFPQ training throws.

## 2026-10-02 - Step 4 - Reassess the implementation plan (pass 1)

Pass 1. New impacts: YES.

I checked the inventory against the tree. I read `ann_ids.py`, `build-ann-index.py`, `embedding_space.py`, the selection and main loop of `precompute-similar-ann.py`, the start-up order in `server.py`, `random_videos.fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, the unfiltered window in `random_cache.populate_random_cache`, the fixtures in `test_video.py`, `test_precompute_similar_ann.py`, `test_random_videos.py` and `test_random_cache.py`, and `tests/config.json`. I also ran a repo-wide search for `rowid`, `random_rowids`, `id_source`, `fetch_random_rowids` and `exclude_rowid`. Every claim I checked matches the file, line numbers included. The other `rowid` hits under `engine/server` and `tests/active` are not ANN ids: the `interaction_events.py` and `users.py` dedupe, the `sync-whitelist.py` FTS triggers, `v.rowid` ordering in `test-moderation-integration.py`, and the `videos.rowid` ordering and FTS helpers in the client and dislike tests. The only things missing from the inventory are about phasing, not code: the readers-first order leaves the phase-1 checkpoint red on every random-cache read until phase 2 lands. The docs `LAYER_PARAMS.md` and `OVERVIEW.md`, which name `random_rowids` and rowids, are not in the inventory, but the plan's AC9 doc list already names them.
<question id="1">
Yes, once all three phases land in the single merge. The writer (`build-ann-index.py:250/252/284`), the gate (`embedding_space.py:79-93`, where the new check fits right after the model check) and all the readers move to one key. The gate's import closure stays stdlib (`ann_ids` → `moderation` → `similarity_cache`), and it is imported only by `server.py`, `build-ann-index.py` and `precompute-similar-ann.py`, all of which already put `engine/server` on `sys.path`.

The plan's claim that "with readers first, no earlier checkpoint goes red" does not hold for the random cache. Phase 1 moves `fetch_metadata` to `WHERE e.ann_id IN`. `random_videos.py:434-441` passes the cache's ids straight into it. But `populate_random_cache` (`random_cache.py:91-103`) keeps writing `rowid` values until phase 2. So at the phase-1 checkpoint, every cache-served random page comes back empty: `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` returns `[]` and the caller falls back to the DB. `test_random_videos`' `_cache_owner` cases fail too, because `_video_db` (line 477) maps labels to `lastrowid`. The single merge means production never sees this. Only the checkpoint does.
</question>
<question id="2">
The ramifications are the ones the inventory lists, and I confirmed them:
- The deploy is a hard cutover. A `rowid` sidecar is refused at `server.py:365` and `precompute-similar-ann.py:345`.
- A failed index build becomes an Engine outage: the updater's `finally` restart hits the gate.
- An old-shape random cache is rebuilt in the background, through `server.py:345`.
- The Engine-backed suite and other lanes are coupled to migrating the shared dataset.
- Rolling back after a reindex gives empty results, not wrong ones.

Two more things follow from reading the code:
- The `rowid` training sampler in `build-ann-index.py:73-81` is untouched, as the plan says.
- The cutover crash window is real. `write_index` (line 271) runs before `meta_path.write_text` (line 286), and the gate refuses the half-written result, so it fails loudly.
</question>
<question id="3">
These must happen beyond what the plan's Approach lists:
- **Test fixtures.** Every fixture the inventory names has to move with its phase, including `test_video.py:218-219` `similars_stack`, which the plan never mentions. The fixtures that turn ids into metadata must move in phase 1, because `fetch_metadata` changes there: `test_video.similars_stack`, `test_metadata._nsfw_metadata`, `test_random_videos._video_db`, and the `INDEX_BUILDER` and column in `test_precompute_similar_ann`.
- **The random-cache seam.** Either the cache's id source moves into phase 1, or the random-cache tests are accepted as red until phase 2 (see Recommendations).
- **The AC4 test** must pass `--nbits`, not just `--nlist`/`--m`/`--train-sample`, because `nbits` defaults to 8 (`build-ann-index.py:178-185`).
- **`tests/config.json`.** `test_db.py` maps only `engine/server/data/db.py` (line 16), and it needs `data/random_cache.py` and `data/ann_ids.py`.
- **Operators.** The shared `whitelist.db` and its index must be migrated and rebuilt before the full suite runs.
</question>
<question id="4">
What users get back does not change. No response carries an id: `seed["meta"]` and the `fetch_metadata` output dicts have none.

What changes:
- **Identity.** FAISS ids and random-cache entries resolve by `ann_id`, so a stale index can only miss, never return the wrong video.
- **Random windows.** An unfiltered random window is a run in hash order, not insertion order.
- **The cache file.** It holds `random_ann_ids(position, ann_id)`. An old `random_rowids` file is treated as missing and rebuilt, even under `--no-random-cache-refresh`.
- **Start-up.** The Engine and the similarity precompute refuse any sidecar whose `id_source` is not `video_embeddings.ann_id`, so they can no longer serve wrong videos from an old index.
- **`build-ann-index.py`** refuses an unmigrated DB with the `migrate-whitelist.py` message.
</question>

New impacts:
engine/server/data/random_videos.py fetch_random_rows_from_cache (lines 434-441) — between phase 1 and phase 2 this passes the `rowid` values that `random_cache.populate_random_cache` still writes (lines 91-103, `INSERT INTO random_rowids (position, video_rowid)` from `SELECT rowid`) into a `fetch_metadata` already filtering on `e.ann_id`. Every cache draw then resolves to nothing, and the random feed falls back to the DB draw. The phase-1 checkpoint therefore fails the cache-served cases in `test_random_videos` (`_cache_owner` / `_video_db` line 477 using `lastrowid`, tests at lines 516-551), the served cases in `test_random_cache` (`_seed_servable_cache` line 196 and `_feed_rowids` line 234 select `rowid`) and `test_db`'s served read. This contradicts the plan's statement that no earlier checkpoint goes red. Production is unaffected because the three phases merge as one unit.

Inventory entries that did not hold up:
none

Conflicts: none

Recommendations: 1. **Close the phase 1 → phase 2 random-cache seam.** Pick one option:
   - **(a) Merge phases 1 and 2 into one phase.** No extra code. The cost is a larger phase, roughly 15 more files at one checkpoint, but it keeps the plan's order and removes the in-between state.
   - **(b) Keep three phases and move only the values early.** Phase 1 changes `populate_random_cache`'s SELECTs to `ann_id` while still writing into `random_rowids.video_rowid`, and moves the random-cache test fixtures' id values to `compute_ann_id`. Phase 2 then renames the table and column. The cost is an intermediate state where the column name lies, plus touching the random-cache fixtures twice.
   - **(c) Accept the red checkpoint** and record those tests as known-red at phase 1. This costs nothing, but it gives up the plan's "no checkpoint goes red" property for that phase.

   I recommend (a). It is the smallest change and stays within the settled single-merge plan. If the operator reads the plan's phasing as settled, treat this as a question for the phasing step rather than a change to the plan.
2. **Pin the phase-1 fixture edits in the phase plan.** Phase 1 must carry `test_video.py:216-219` `similars_stack` (`SELECT ann_id` / `r["ann_id"]`; the plan does not name it), `test_metadata._nsfw_metadata`, and `test_precompute_similar_ann`'s column, `INDEX_BUILDER` and sidecar `id_source`, all together. The cost is fixture churn only, with no product code involved.
3. **Pass `--cpu` and a small `--nbits` in the AC4 test**, as the inventory already notes. Plan text only; no cost.
4. **Add `engine/server/data/random_cache.py` and `engine/server/data/ann_ids.py` to `test_db.py` in `tests/config.json`.** Today it maps only `data/db.py` (line 16). The cost is two lines.
5. **Rewrite the doc lines on the AC9 checklist.** `LAYER_PARAMS.md:130` says a start builds when the cache "has no `random_rowids` table". Line 140, plus `OVERVIEW.md:15` and `:69`, say "rowids". These must be rewritten, not just appended to. Line 130 should say that an old `random_rowids` file now counts as missing and triggers a build even with refresh off. ### impacts


<impact path="engine/server/data/ann_ids.py" element="new module constant ANN_ID_SOURCE">
**What changes.** I read the module as delivered. It holds `ANN_ID_MASK`, `compute_ann_id`, `create_video_embeddings_table`, `create_ann_id_guards`, `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id` and `ensure_video_embeddings_schema`. It has **no** `ANN_ID_SOURCE` yet, so the plan's new one-string constant (`"video_embeddings.ann_id"`) is added here. It needs a one-line comment in the file's style.

**What depends on it.** Three new importers:
- `build-ann-index.py`, which writes the constant into the sidecar.
- `embedding_space.py`, which gates on it.
- `test-orchestrator-smoke.py`, which asserts on it.

Probably also the new AC5 and AC8 tests.

**Import chain.** The module imports `data.moderation`, which imports `data.similarity_cache`. Both are stdlib only. Importing it from `embedding_space.py` therefore adds that chain to the Engine's and both jobs' import graph. There is no cycle: `moderation` and `similarity_cache` never import `embedding_space`.

**Regression risk.** Low. If anyone adds numpy or faiss here, `test_precompute_random_rowids.py` breaks, because it runs the job under `sys.executable`. The constant must stay byte-identical to what readers compare against. One source of truth removes the risk of a typo in two places.
</impact>
<impact path="engine/server/db/jobs/build-ann-index.py" element="main(): old-shape guard after sqlite3.connect (line 212), add query (line 250), ids array (line 252), meta id_source (line 284), imports (line 20)">
**What changes.**

**Regression risk.** Medium to high.

- `ann_id` ≤ 2^63-1 fits int64. No negative id is possible: `CHECK > 0` holds, and FAISS uses -1 for empty slots.

**What changes.** Nothing. It keeps `SELECT rowid ... WHERE (rowid % ?) = 0`, as the plan's named simplification.

**What depends on it.** `main()` uses it for quantizer training only, never for identity.

**Regression risk.** None for correctness; recall only. Its local loop variable is named `rowid`, so the rename grep will flag it. The implementer must leave it, and the reviewer must not treat it as a missed rename.

**AC4 test concern.** IVFPQ training with `--nbits 8` needs at least 256 training points per PQ codebook. With fewer, faiss fails `nx >= k`. A fixture of "a few dozen vectors" must therefore pass a small `--nbits` (for example 4), or carry at least 256 vectors. It must also pass `--nlist` ≤ the sample count and an `--m` that divides dim. The plan names `--nlist`, `--m` and `--train-sample` but not `--nbits`.
</impact>

The message names the index's source (or `<unset>`), says the readers resolve `video_embeddings.ann_id`, and says "Rebuild the index with build-ann-index.py."

`build-ann-index.py` imports `resolve_embedding_space` from this module, which now also loads `data.ann_ids`.

**Regression risk.** High, operationally. Every existing sidecar (live `whitelist-video-embeddings.faiss.json`, `id_source: video_embeddings.rowid`) is refused, and so is every test sidecar without `id_source`. That includes `tests/active/test_precompute_similar_ann.py:74`, and the session `engine` fixture fails on the shared dataset until it is rebuilt.

**Placement.** The check runs before the dim checks, so a rowid index with the right model and dim is refused for the id first. Keep it after the model check, as the plan says. Otherwise the existing model-mismatch messages, which operators and docs rely on, would be pre-empted by an id message on a model-change index. Order matters only for which message appears.

<impact path="engine/server/data/random_cache.py" element="populate_random_cache() (lines 51-194): existing count/DELETE (71, 74), source stats (75-78), unfiltered window (90-106), filtered try_add/scan_range (108-192)">
**What changes.**
- `existing`/`DELETE` move to `random_ann_ids`.
- The stats become `COUNT(*), MIN(ann_id), MAX(ann_id)`, and `random.randint(min_id, max_id)` now spans a 63-bit range (Python ints are fine).
- The unfiltered window: `SELECT ann_id FROM video_embeddings WHERE ann_id >= ? ORDER BY ann_id LIMIT ?`, plus the wrap `ann_id < ?`.
- Inserts: `INSERT INTO random_ann_ids (position, ann_id)`.
- `try_add` reads `entry["ann_id"]`.
- `scan_range` selects `e.ann_id AS ann_id`, filters `e.ann_id >= ? AND e.ann_id <= ? ORDER BY e.ann_id`, and advances with `current = int(rows[-1]["ann_id"]) + 1`.
- The locals become `ann_ids`, and a comment notes the hash-uniform window.

**What depends on it.**
- `build_random_cache`, behind `refresh_random_cache` and `run_random_cache_worker`: the Engine's background builds.
- `precompute-random-rowids.py`.
- `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` (in-process populate at line 311), `test_db.py` and `test_precompute_random_rowids.py`. All their sources are 2-column `video_embeddings` tables without `ann_id`, so all need the column.

**Regression risk.** Medium.
- The keyset scan advances by `ann_id + 1`; at the maximum 2^63-1 that would overflow SQLite's int64 binding. `current` is only advanced after a row ≤ `range_end` = `max_id`, and the loop condition `current <= range_end` stops it. But if `max_id == 2**63-1`, `+1` yields a Python int above int64. The comparison happens in Python first, so no bind occurs. Safe, but worth a glance.
- Unfiltered draw distribution changes from insertion-order blocks to hash-uniform, as the plan accepts.
- Tests that asserted "positions 1..20 over rowids 1..20" now need the set of 20 computed ids.
</impact>

### highest_risk


engine/server/data/ann.py search_similar_above() / compute_similar_items() together with engine/server/data/embeddings.py resolve_seed/_seed_from_row: in a partial seed-key rename, `seed.get("rowid")` silently stops up-next self-exclusion. Neither `test_similarity_candidates`, whose stub replaces it, nor any non-Engine test catches it. `seed["rowid"]` and `seed["exclude_rowid"]` raise KeyError on every similar or vector request.
engine/server/db/jobs/build-ann-index.py add query and ids array: a `rowid` left in the add path writes a rowid-keyed index under an `ann_id` sidecar. The new gate accepts it, and every hit becomes a wrong video. Only an AC4 test that compares `index.id_map` with the DB's `ann_id` set catches it, and that test also needs a small `--nbits` (or ≥256 vectors) for IVFPQ to train on a tiny fixture.
scripts/worktree-setup.sh shared symlinked whitelist-video-embeddings.faiss and .json, with tests/active/conftest.py's engine fixture: the gate refuses the shared rowid sidecar, so the Engine-backed suite fails in this worktree. Rebuilding the index from here overwrites main's index through the symlink, and main's ungated rowid readers then serve misses or wrong videos. The dataset cutover must be coordinated with the merge.

## 2026-10-02 - Step 4 - Reassess the implementation plan (pass 2)

Pass 2. New impacts: YES.

I opened the files behind the inventory. The plan holds, and the inventory is accurate on the code. These all match the tree: `ann_ids.py` has no `ANN_ID_SOURCE` yet; `build-ann-index.py` lines 20, 52, 58, 75-83, 212-215, 250-252 and 284; the model-then-dim order in `embedding_space.py`; the `rowid` readers in `ann.py`, `embeddings.py`, `metadata.py`, `search.py` and `similar.py`; every `random_rowids`/`video_rowid` site in `random_cache.py` and its two importers; the `precompute-similar-ann.py` selection and target code; and the updater order, where the ANN build runs before the similarity precompute. Two points the inventory left open now check out. `test_internal_client_reads.py` only drives the metadata and centroids handlers (`HANDLERS`, line 75), so it never reaches the resolve route. `test_search.py`'s stub sets `query_encoder=None` (line 68), so `vector_candidates` returns before it calls `fetch_metadata`. Nothing outside `engine/server` reads an id key: `client/` has no ANN-id or random-cache reader. I found two things the inventory does not carry. First, the cutover meets the blue/green deploy and the in-place index write, and that is not covered. Second, two lines in the recommendation docs that name rowids are missing from the doc list. I also found that one claim recurring in the inventory overstates the failure mode: a rowid/ann_id mismatch empties the results, it does not serve wrong videos.
<question id="1">Yes. Every reader of a FAISS id resolves `video_embeddings.ann_id` through one function, `fetch_metadata`, which is served by plan A's UNIQUE index. The build writes the same ids, and the gate in `assert_index_matches_embeddings` covers both index consumers (`server.py:365`, `precompute-similar-ann.py:345`). Both consumers read the sidecar before any `ann_id` query. Training on `rowid % step` stays correct, because `whitelist_migrations.py:401` keeps rowids and a new-shape table is still a rowid table. Plain FAISS refuses to train on too few points, so the AC4 test must pass a small `--nbits` (the inventory already notes this). That is a test parameter, not a gap in the plan.</question>
<question id="2">This is a hard cutover, and the Engine refuses a rowid sidecar. One consequence the inventory misses: `build-ann-index.py:271` writes the index in place at `--index-path`. The blue/green flow (`scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh`) starts the new instance while the old one keeps serving. So the cutover cannot go through it without either a refused new instance (a readiness rollback, which is safe) or a rebuild that overwrites the file the old instance has memory-mapped (`IO_FLAG_MMAP`, `server.py:350`). The cutover is therefore a manual stop/build/start on the active unit, with the updater kept out. Both colours share `random-cache.db`. During an overlap the old colour's next refresh writes back a `random_rowids` file, and the new code just rebuilds it again; this is harmless and corrects itself. A mismatch between the readers' ids and the index's ids makes nearly every hit miss: an `ann_id` is a 63-bit hash with `CHECK > 0`, and a rowid is small. The gate therefore prevents silently empty results, not wrong videos.</question>
<question id="3">Beyond the inventory, the documented cutover must name the exact sequence. Hold the deploy lock, or make sure `peertube-engine-updater` is not running. Stop the active `peertube-engine@<port>`. Run `build-ann-index.py` against the migrated `whitelist.db`. Start the same unit. Do not run `deploy-bluegreen.sh` for this one release. Two doc lines also need updating: `LAYER_PARAMS.md:140` and `OVERVIEW.md:69`. Everything else the inventory lists still applies: the test fixtures, the `id_source` in the `test_precompute_similar_ann` sidecar landing in phase 1, `tests/config.json`, and rebuilding the shared index only after main merges.</question>
<question id="4">The responses do not change. What changes: the Engine refuses an index whose sidecar is not `ann_id`. Old random caches are treated as `no_table` and rebuilt in the background. The unfiltered random window becomes a hash-uniform window instead of a block in insertion order. The log key changes from `ann_rowids=` to `ann_ids=`. `fetch_metadata` now looks ids up through a secondary UNIQUE index instead of the rowid primary key. A stale index now misses (purged or new videos), and re-embedded videos still resolve correctly. Before, a rowid shift could point a hit at another row. One more change: until the cutover, this release cannot use the zero-downtime blue/green path.</question>

New impacts:
scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh — The cutover release cannot go through blue/green. Steps 5-6 start the new colour while the old one serves. A new colour on a rowid sidecar fails the gate and rolls back at readiness, which is safe. Rebuilding first is the problem: `build-ann-index.py:271` calls `faiss.write_index` in place at the shared `whitelist-video-embeddings.faiss`, while the old colour has that file mapped with `IO_FLAG_MMAP` (`server.py:350`). The rewrite truncates and refills the mapped file under a live process, so the old colour can read garbage or take a SIGBUS. The documented cutover therefore has to bypass this script: stop the active `peertube-engine@<port>`, build, start the same unit.
engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py — The manual cutover build and the updater's own ANN stage (lines 1388-1409, run under the deploy lock it takes) write the same index path. If the operator does not hold `LOCK_FILE`, or check that the updater unit is inactive, two builds can interleave index and sidecar writes. The cutover sequence must take the deploy lock, or check the updater state the way `deploy-bluegreen.sh` step 2 does.
engine/server/data/random_cache.py — Blue/green colours share `DB_DIR/random-cache.db` (`deploy-bluegreen.sh:207-214`). If a pre-B colour and a B colour run at once, the old colour's interval refresh renames a `random_rowids` file over the new `random_ann_ids` one. Each Engine keeps serving from its own inode, and the next B start logs `no_table` and rebuilds. This is harmless and self-healing, but the docs should name it so an operator does not take the `no_table` line for a fault.
engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md — Line 140 ("The cache holds only rowids (`random_rowids`) … when a draw's rowids are resolved") also describes the old cache shape. The requirements' doc list covers only line 130 of this file.
engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md — Line 69 ("Holds a prebuilt list of rowids for quick random pools") goes stale. The requirements' doc list covers only line 15 of this file.

Inventory entries that did not hold up:
engine/server/db/jobs/build-ann-index.py (main, the add-query entry) — It claims that a missed `rowid` in the add query writes a rowid-keyed index that "the gate then accepts and every hit is a wrong video". The code does not support that. `ann_ids.py:10-18` masks each id to a 63-bit blake2b value with `CHECK (ann_id > 0)`, and rowids are dense small integers. A rowid looked up as an `ann_id` in `fetch_metadata` hits only when it equals some video's hash, a chance of about N/2^63 per lookup. The real failure is silently empty similar, search and random results, not wrong videos. The AC4 `id_map` equality test is still needed, and the risk is still silent, but its symptom is emptiness.
scripts/worktree-setup.sh — It says that a shared index rebuilt from a worktree makes main's code "resolve ann_id hits as rowids: misses, or wrong videos". For the same reason, it is in practice misses only, up to that same negligible collision chance. The coordination risk stands, but the symptom is empty results on main and on the other worktrees.
engine/server/api/handlers/internal_client_reads.py — The entry left its test unverified. It is now confirmed: `tests/active/test_internal_client_reads.py:75` maps only `metadata` and `centroids`, so the resolve route is never exercised. This settles the entry rather than contradicting it.
tests/active/test_search.py — The entry left the stub unverified. It is now confirmed: line 68 builds `SimpleNamespace(db=..., db_lock=..., query_encoder=None)`, so `vector_candidates` returns at `search.py:185`. This settles the entry rather than contradicting it.

Conflicts: none

Recommendations: 1. Write the exact cutover sequence into the DEPLOYMENT.md change the plan already makes at line 42. Take the deploy lock, or confirm `peertube-engine-updater` is inactive. Run `systemctl stop peertube-engine@<active port>`. Run `build-ann-index.py --db-path <migrated whitelist.db> --normalize --cpu|--gpu` to the live paths. Run `systemctl start peertube-engine@<same port>`. State that `deploy-bluegreen.sh` must not be used for this release. Add a triage note that `random cache unusable … reason=no_table` is expected once after the upgrade. Cost: a few doc lines and no code. Downtime equals one index build. The Engine's similar, search and random reads are down for that time; the Client's own routes are unaffected.
2. Optional, and outside the settled plan, so take it only if zero-downtime matters: make `build-ann-index.py` write the index and the sidecar to temp files beside their targets and `os.replace` them into place, index first. The old colour keeps its mapped inode, and with it its consistent rowid view, so the cutover can run as rebuild then `deploy-bluegreen.sh`. Updater runs also lose their in-place write. Cost: about six lines in `build-ann-index.py`, one more AC4 assertion that no temp file is left, and a second copy of the index on disk until the old colour stops. It changes neither the crash-window analysis (the gate still refuses a mismatched pair) nor any reader.
3. Add `LAYER_PARAMS.md:140` and `OVERVIEW.md:69` to the doc edits. Cost: two sentences.
4. In the docs and in the gate's docstring paragraph, describe a wrong id source as "silently empty results" rather than "wrong videos". That is the real symptom, and it tells an operator what to look for. Cost: none. The gate stays as planned.
5. When writing the AC4 test, keep the inventory's note: pass `--nbits 4`, or seed at least 256 vectors, plus `--nlist` no larger than the sample count and an `--m` that divides the dimension. Otherwise FAISS training aborts before the code under test runs. Cost: none beyond the test's arguments.

**What changes:** nothing (named simplification). It still runs `SELECT rowid ... WHERE (rowid % ?) = 0`. On a table rebuilt by plan A's migration, rowids were copied, so they are still contiguous. On a fresh sync-whitelist table they are also contiguous.

**What depends on it:** the AC4 test. The test passes small `--train-sample`, `--nlist` and `--m`. The plan does not mention one constraint here: `IndexIVFPQ` with the default `--nbits 8` trains 256 centroids per sub-quantizer, and FAISS clustering raises when there are fewer training points than centroids. A fixture of "a few dozen vectors" therefore also needs a small `--nbits` (e.g. 4 gives 16 centroids, or ≥256 rows). It also needs `dim % m == 0` (line 107) and `nlist` ≤ the number of training vectors.

**Regression risk:** none to production. The test-parameter trap above is the risk to AC4.

- `ann_id + 1` cannot overflow, because MAX ≤ 2^63-1 ends the loop via `current <= range_end` before any increment past the max. `rows[-1]["ann_id"] + 1` can still reach 2^63 as a Python int and is then bound as a parameter on the next loop test. That does not happen because the loop condition `current <= range_end` is checked first in Python. Flagged anyway: binding 2^63 to SQLite would raise OverflowError, so do not reorder the loop.
</impact>

<impact path="tests/active/test_ann_ids.py" element="NEW: AC4 build-ann-index job test and AC5 gate cases">
**What changes:** a new file. It runs `build-ann-index.py --cpu` under `ENGINE_PY` on a tmp DB built through `ensure_video_embeddings_schema`, then loads the index in an `ENGINE_PY` child and compares `faiss.vector_to_array(index.id_map)` with the DB's `ann_id` set. It runs AC5 against the written sidecar, a `rowid` sidecar and one with no `id_source`, using a stub index with `.d`.

The parameters must satisfy:
- `dim % m == 0`;
- training count ≥ `nlist`;
- training count ≥ 2^`nbits` (pass a small `--nbits`, see the `fetch_training_samples` entry);
- `--train-sample` ≥ rows, so `step` = 1.

It must pass explicit `--index-path` and `--meta-path` in tmp, or it overwrites `engine/server/db/video-embeddings.faiss`.

**What depends on it:** AC4/AC5.

**Regression risk:** none to production. Register it in `tests/config.json`.
</impact>

### highest_risk


1. `engine/server/data/embeddings.py` + `engine/server/data/ann.py` + `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py` (seed keys `rowid`/`exclude_rowid` → `ann_id`/`exclude_ann_id`): the producer and three readers must rename together. A leftover `seed["exclude_rowid"]` 500s vector search. A leftover `seed.get("rowid")` in `search_similar_above` silently drops self-exclusion from up-next. No type check catches either, only tests that assert self-exclusion.
2. The shared dataset and index cutover (`scripts/worktree-setup.sh` symlinks + `engine/server/data/embedding_space.py` gate + `tests/active/conftest.py` engine fixture): after phase 3 every Engine start on the current `rowid` sidecar refuses, so the whole Engine-backed suite goes red. Rebuilding from this worktree rewrites main's live index. Main has no gate and resolves by rowid, so main would serve empty similar and search results until it merges this build. `build-ann-index.py`'s default output paths also do not match the served index.
3. `tests/active/test_random_cache.py::test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy` (plus the checkout's copied old-shape `random-cache.db`): the plan's churn list misses it. It reads `random_rowids` from the checkout cache (lines 691, 706). The session Engine now finds that cache unusable and runs a background 500k build, so the test either hits "no such table: random_ann_ids" before the build lands or fails its `cached_rows < DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_SIZE` control after it lands. Eight refresh-off Engines would also each start a build, against the test's premise.

```python
RANDOM_CACHE_CHECK_SQL = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM random_ann_ids"

def ensure_random_cache_schema(conn):
    conn.executescript("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS random_ann_ids (
          position INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          ann_id INTEGER NOT NULL
        );
        """)

def random_ann_ids_count(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int | None:
    """Return the number of cached ANN ids, or None when the random_ann_ids table is missing, as in a cache written before the ANN-id cutover (random_rowids)."""
    # fetchall, so no statement is left holding SHARED on the file.
    if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'random_ann_ids' LIMIT 1").fetchall():
        return None
    return int(conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM random_ann_ids").fetchall()[0][0])
```
`populate_random_cache`:
- The reuse check uses `random_ann_ids_count`, and the count and delete run on `random_ann_ids`.
- The source stats query is `SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, MIN(ann_id) AS min_id, MAX(ann_id) AS max_id FROM video_embeddings`.

- The insert is `INSERT INTO random_ann_ids (position, ann_id) VALUES (?, ?)` with `int(row["ann_id"])`.
- Filtered: the local list `rowids` becomes `ann_ids`, and `try_add` reads `entry["ann_id"]`. `scan_range` selects `e.ann_id AS ann_id`, uses `WHERE e.ann_id >= ? AND e.ann_id <= ? ORDER BY e.ann_id`, and advances with `current = int(rows[-1]["ann_id"]) + 1`.

The parameters are chosen so that 8 % 2 == 0, 64 ≥ nlist, 64 ≥ 2^4, and step is 1. The explicit paths avoid touching `engine/server/db/video-embeddings.faiss`.

#### `tests/active/test_stale_ann_index.py` (phase 1, AC8)
- **The outer process builds the DB.** Like `test_video.py`, it loads `sync-whitelist.py` through `spec_from_file_location`, calls `ensure_whitelist_schema` and `ensure_content_schema` (which create `video_embeddings` with `ann_id` and its guards), and inserts 12 videos into `videos`, each with `last_checked_at`, a `channel_id` and `nsfw` 0. Hosts: v0..v7 on `keep.example` and v8..v11 on `purge.example`. Embeddings are `DIM=4`, with distinct vectors from a fixed `math.cos`/`sin` formula and `ann_id=compute_ann_id(...)`.
- **The ENGINE_PY child.** It sets `sys.path[:0] = [server, server/api]` and builds `IDMap2,IVF1,Flat`, `METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT`, from `SELECT ann_id, embedding`. That search is exact. It records `recorded = {ann_id: (video_id, host)}`. Then, per case, it copies the DB with `shutil.copy` and mutates the copy without rebuilding the index:
  - **A:** `rows = SELECT * FROM video_embeddings ORDER BY rowid`, then `DELETE`, then reinsert `reversed(rows)`. A control asserts that the rowid→key mapping changed.
  - **B:** `purge_host_data(conn, "purge.example")`.
  - **C:** insert video `new` on `keep.example` whose vector equals the probe, with its computed `ann_id`.
- **The stub server.** `SimpleNamespace(index, index_lock, db, db_lock, normalize_queries=False, similarity_search_limit=0, similarity_exclude_source_author=False, similarity_max_per_author=0, video_error_threshold=None, query_encoder=SimpleNamespace(enabled=True, encode=lambda text: probe))`.
- **The seed.** `embeddings.resolve_seed(conn, 4, None, "v0", "keep.example", None)`, which exercises the producer rename. The probe is v0's vector.
- **Expected results**, with `present = {SELECT ann_id}` and limit 50, which is greater than N:
  - similar: `[recorded[i] for i in index.search(probe, 51) ids if i > 0 and i != seed_ann_id and i in present]`;
  - search: the same list without the self-exclusion, over `search_index`'s first `limit` unique ids.
- **The child prints, per case,** the actual similar and search keys next to the expected ones. The outer test asserts:
  - actual == expected, and expected is non-empty (control);
  - in case B, no `purge.example` key appears, and a control shows the host had hits before the purge;
  - in case C, `("new", "keep.example")` appears in neither list.
- A reader still joining on rowid would return nothing for 63-bit ids, and a rowid-keyed index would be permuted by case A. The equality check fails either way.

### Phasing
All three phases merge together. Each checkpoint stays green when the next phase lands.
1. **Readers and similarity precompute.** Checkpoint: `test_stale_ann_index`, `test_precompute_similar_ann` (its sidecar already carries `id_source`), `test_metadata`, and `test_video` similars.
2. **Random cache.** Checkpoint: `test_precompute_random_rowids` including `old_shape`, `test_random_cache` in-process cases, `test_db`, `test_random_videos`.
3. **`ANN_ID_SOURCE`, index build, gate, smoke assertion, docs.** Checkpoint: `test_ann_ids`.

### Decisions and named simplifications
- **Training samples** keep `rowid % step`. Ceiling: recall only. Upgrade: one token, `ann_id % step`.
- **Old-cache detection** is by table name. Ceiling: a reshape under the same name. Upgrade: a `PRAGMA table_info` check in `random_ann_ids_count`.
- **No startup DB-shape check** (AC5 does not ask for one). Upgrade: `assert_video_embeddings_has_ann_id(db)` next to `server.py:346`.

### Operator coordination (from the inventory, made concrete)
- **Shared files.** The worktree's `whitelist.db` and `whitelist-video-embeddings.faiss[.json]` are symlinks to main's live files. Rebuilding them from here would switch main to `ann_id` ids before main has the readers. The full suite after phase 3 therefore needs either a coordinated main cutover or private copies in the worktree.
- **The engines test** (`test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy`) needs a short new-shape cache, or its premise does not hold. The old-shape copied `random-cache.db` makes the session Engine run a background build of up to 500k rows, which can fail its "short cache" control. Before the suite, run `precompute-random-rowids.py --refresh` (default `--size 5000`) on the worktree's own `engine/server/db/random-cache.db` copy, after the dataset migration.
- **The smoke test** needs a migrated `--source-db` and is run manually.

Needs coordination: Phase 4 (full-suite close): the worktree's `whitelist.db` and `whitelist-video-embeddings.faiss[.json]` are symlinks to main's live files. Before the full suite runs, the operator must either coordinate a main cutover (stop the Engine, run `migrate-whitelist.py`, then `build-ann-index.py` onto the served paths, then start) or give the worktree private copies. Otherwise the gate refuses the rowid sidecar and the Engine-backed suite goes red. Also before the full suite, after the migration: run `precompute-random-rowids.py --refresh` on the worktree's own `engine/server/db/random-cache.db` copy, so the engines test (`test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy`) has a short new-shape cache. Phase 4's smoke-test assertion: `test-orchestrator-smoke.py` needs a migrated `--source-db` and is run manually by the operator.

Rationale: This follows the settled order of readers, then random cache, then index build and gate. With that order, no earlier checkpoint goes red when a later phase lands, because phase 1 already writes `id_source` into the `test_precompute_similar_ann` fixture sidecar. Phase 1 keeps the whole seed and reader rename as one unit, since a partial rename silently breaks self-exclusion. Its two clauses are the live readers (AC8) and the offline precompute (AC7). Phase 2 is the random cache, which has its own table and job, and old-shape handling (AC6). The draft's phase 3 carried three observable facts: the id set plus sidecar, the refusal of old tables, and the gate. The two-clause rule therefore splits it into phase 3, the index build (AC4), and phase 4, the gate (AC5) plus the manual smoke assertion (AC9). They share the `test_ann_ids.py` harness, with phase 4 reusing the sidecar phase 3 builds. All phases merge together, as settled. The docs and the issue archiving are documentation and go to Step 9, so there is no prose phase. The operator approved this four-phase breakdown.
